title_py: Gèng duō shíwù: mǐfàn, niúnǎi hé miànbāo
auditory_note: Tap ▶ Listen to play each clip.

intro.en: Hi Evan! Today we keep going with food. You will meet rice, milk, and bread, and use them with chī and hē. Your older words (names, ages, pets, colors, and numbers) come back in new sentences and little chats, so each one gets stronger. Say every line out loud.
intro.py: Nǐ hǎo, Evan! Jīntiān wǒmen jìxù xué shíwù. Nǐ huì rènshi mǐfàn, niúnǎi hé miànbāo, bìng hé chī, hē yìqǐ yòng. Nǐ yǐqián xué de cí (míngzi, niánlíng, chǒngwù, yánsè hé shùzì) huì chūxiàn zài xīn de jùzi hé duǎn duìhuà lǐ, ràng měi gè cí gèng jiāngù. Měi jù dōu dàshēng shuō.

blocks.text: More food: rice, milk and bread

blocks.en: Last time you learned to eat, to drink, water, and apple. Today we add three everyday foods: rice, milk, and bread. Each one slots straight into the same two sentences, Wǒ chī… and Wǒ hē…. Notice that rice and bread go with chī (eat), and milk goes with hē (drink).
blocks.py: Shàng cì nǐ xuéle chī, hē, shuǐ hé píngguǒ. Jīntiān wǒmen zài xué sān zhǒng rìcháng shíwù: mǐfàn, niúnǎi hé miànbāo. Tāmen dōu kěyǐ fàng jìn tóngyàng de liǎng gè jùzi: Wǒ chī… hé Wǒ hē…. Zhùyì, mǐfàn hé miànbāo yòng chī, niúnǎi yòng hē.

blocks.note_en: Mǐ is 3rd tone and fàn is 4th: dip, then drop sharply. Rice is the classic food word. Wǒ chī mǐfàn = I eat rice.
blocks.note_py: Mǐ shì 3rd tone, fàn shì 4th tone: xiān dī, zài zhòng jiàng. Wǒ chī mǐfàn jiùshì I eat rice.

blocks.note_en: Niú is 2nd tone (rising), nǎi is 3rd (dip). Literally "cow milk". Wǒ hē niúnǎi = I drink milk. Great one to say with the kids.
blocks.note_py: Niú shì 2nd tone, nǎi shì 3rd tone. Zìmiàn yìsi shì "niú de nǎi". Wǒ hē niúnǎi jiùshì I drink milk.

blocks.note_en: Miàn is 4th tone, bāo is 1st: drop, then high and flat. Wǒ chī miànbāo = I eat bread.
blocks.note_py: Miàn shì 4th tone, bāo shì 1st tone: xiān jiàng, zài gāo ér píng. Wǒ chī miànbāo jiùshì I eat bread.

blocks.en: Now we mix the new foods with words you already know: your pets, your kids, colors, and numbers. Listen to each line and say it out loud. Watch for old friends like māo, gǒu, háizi, hóngsè, and zhī.
blocks.py: Xiànzài bǎ xīn shíwù hé nǐ yǐjīng zhīdào de cí fàng zài yìqǐ: chǒngwù, háizi, yánsè hé shùzì. Měi jù xiān tīng zài shuō. Zhùyì māo, gǒu, háizi, hóngsè hé zhī zhèxiē lǎo péngyou.

blocks.en: The cat drinks milk, but it doesn't eat bread.
blocks.py: Māo hē niúnǎi, kěshì bù chī miànbāo.

blocks.en: I have two apples and one bread.
blocks.py: Wǒ yǒu liǎng gè píngguǒ hé yí gè miànbāo.

blocks.en: What is your name? My name is Evan. How old are you?
blocks.py: Nǐ jiào shénme míngzi? Wǒ jiào Evan. Nǐ jǐ suì?
Báisè de gǒu xǐhuan chī mǐfàn.

blocks.title: Pattern: eat vs. drink
blocks.body_en: Solid food goes with chī (eat): mǐfàn, miànbāo, píngguǒ. Liquids go with hē (drink): shuǐ, niúnǎi. If you pick the wrong verb it sounds funny, just like in English.
blocks.body_py: Gùtǐ shíwù yòng chī: mǐfàn, miànbāo, píngguǒ. Yètǐ yòng hē: shuǐ, niúnǎi. Dòngcí yòng cuò jiù huì hěn qíguài, hé yīngwén yíyàng.

blocks.en: Use shénme (what) to ask what someone eats or drinks, and ma to ask yes or no. Then answer with bù (no) plus the verb, or with a full sentence. Here are two short conversations.
blocks.py: Yòng shénme wèn biérén chī shénme, hē shénme, yòng ma wèn shì bú shì. Huídá kěyǐ shuō bù jiā dòngcí, yě kěyǐ shuō wánzhěng de jùzi. Xiàmiàn shì liǎng duàn duǎn duìhuà.

blocks.note_en: Ma goes at the very end to turn a statement into a yes/no question. Answer: Hē. (yes) or Wǒ bù hē. (no).
blocks.note_py: Ma fàng zài jù wěi biàn chéng yí-bù-yí wèn jù. Huídá: Hē. huò Wǒ bù hē.

blocks.title: Mini-chats
blocks.body_en: A: What do you eat? B: I eat rice. A: Does your child drink milk? B: Yes, my child drinks milk. A: How old is your child? B: He is four.
blocks.body_py: A: Nǐ chī shénme? B: Wǒ chī mǐfàn. A: Nǐ de háizi hē niúnǎi ma? B: Hē, wǒ de háizi hē niúnǎi. A: Nǐ de háizi jǐ suì? B: Tā sì suì.

pairs.en: What do you eat? I eat rice.
pairs.py: Nǐ chī shénme? Wǒ chī mǐfàn.

pairs.en: Does your child drink milk? Yes. How old is he? He is four.
pairs.py: Nǐ de háizi hē niúnǎi ma? Hē. Tā jǐ suì? Tā sì suì.

blocks.title: Say it at the table
blocks.body_en: At breakfast, name what you and the kids eat and drink: Wǒ hē shuǐ, Wǒ chī miànbāo, Nǐ hē niúnǎi ma? Say yí gè píngguǒ or liǎng gè miànbāo when you count. Saying old words in real places is the fastest way to remember them.
blocks.body_py: Zǎofàn shí, shuō shuo nǐ hé háizi chī shénme, hē shénme: Wǒ hē shuǐ, Wǒ chī miànbāo, Nǐ hē niúnǎi ma? Shǔ shù shí shuō yí gè píngguǒ huò liǎng gè miànbāo. Zài zhēnshí de dìfang shuō lǎo cí, zuì róngyì jì zhù.

practice.how_to: Type your answers in the boxes below. Use tone marks on every pinyin answer (missing tones earn half credit). For 🎤 S1–S3, record a short clip on this page (you can replay and re-record; each clip stops at about 20 seconds). Then tap Submit to see your written score right away.

Say what you drink, in a full pinyin sentence.

intro_callout.title: Record each clip right on this page
intro_callout.body_en: Listen to each model first, then record S1–S3. Remember: in S3, nǐ jiào sounds like ní jiào.
intro_callout.body_py: Xiān tīng, ránhòu lùyīn S1 dào S3. S3 lǐ nǐ jiào shuō chéng ní jiào.

closing.en: Great work, Evan! Today, say Wǒ hē niúnǎi or Wǒ chī miànbāo out loud once at a meal. Tap Submit when your written answers and voice clips are ready. Jiāyóu!
closing.py: Zuò de hěn hǎo, Evan! Jīntiān chīfàn de shíhou, dàshēng shuō yí biàn Wǒ hē niúnǎi huò Wǒ chī miànbāo. Nǐ zhǔnbèi hǎo xiěxià de dá'àn hé yǔyīn le, jiù diǎn Submit. Jiāyóu!

expected: Wǒ de háizi xǐhuan chī píngguǒ.
